current_evidence: Not verified: the shared WebFetch budget (400/hour) and the per-turn WebSearch budget were both exhausted before any council page could be fetched, so the live page and any post-July-2024 revision could not be checked; the issues below come only from Grokbot's own extracted text.

issues.detail: Householder is set to '(none)' (national requirements only), but Grokbot's own extracted triggers name householder-type work. The Contaminated Land trigger explicitly covers 'an extension to a residential property'. The tree survey trigger covers any development affecting trees on or next to the site. Flood Risk Assessment applies to any development in Flood Zones 2/3. The plan standards (block plan at 1:500, scale bar, no 'Do Not Scale') also apply to every application type.
issues.evidence: Contaminated land trigger: 'applications which involve the creation of new dwellinghouse, an extension to a residential property or commercial redevelopment with an area greater than 250m2 will need to be accompanied by a desk-top study'

issues.detail: 18 of 23 requirement rows are under Full planning with the note 'INFERRED: application type not named ... placed under Full planning'. As a result, every other type except LBC (D&A) and Advertisement shows '(none)'. Examples: the HRA/Solent recreation/nutrient neutrality trigger is 'any development creating new dwellinghouses, hotel bedspaces, or other use that increases overnight stays', which also covers Outline and change-of-use prior approvals to residential. The D&A trigger (major, one or more dwellings, 100 sqm or more, listed buildings) also covers Outline. Air quality, tree and flood triggers are location-based, not tied to the application type.
issues.evidence: app_type_rows notes: 'INFERRED: application type not named in extracted text of a general local list; placed under Full planning - check source for applicability' (18 rows)

issues.detail: Several trigger excerpts are tail fragments that leave out when the requirement applies. Habitats Regulations Assessment: 'and the Solent Recreation Mitigation Strategy.' (the real trigger about new dwellings, hotel bedspaces and overnight stays is in tab_items but not in the row). Parking: 'SPD on Parking Standards and Transport Assessments.' Transport Assessment: 'Standards and Transport Assessments.' Planning Statement: 'the accompanying planning statement.' (this is really from the retail sequential-test requirement). Viability: 'to supply a viability assessment produced by a suitably qualified expert.' Archaeology starts mid-sentence. Air Quality is cut off at 'such information a'.
issues.evidence: app_type_rows trigger_excerpt values for HRA, Parking provision, Transport Assessment, Planning Statement, Viability Assessment, Archaeological Assessment, Air Quality Assessment

issues.detail: Two rows are filed under the wrong requirement name. 'Existing and proposed site levels / sections' quotes text about showing floor area with headroom of at least 1.5m, which is a floorspace-measurement or HMO room-size requirement, not site levels. 'Floor plans / Elevations' quotes the HMO-specific rule (internal layout of every room plus a schedule of gross internal floor areas) as if it applied to all full applications. The HMO trigger should be its own requirement for HMO change-of-use applications.
issues.evidence: 'include elevations, cross-sections and plans to show the floor area with a headroom of at least 1.5m.'; 'Multiple Occupancy, floor plans must show the internal layout of that accommodation and every room within it...'

issues.detail: The CIL Additional Information form row has no trigger, only 'submit the CIL additional information form alongside their planning application'. It also keeps the hedge 'only where council is a CIL charging authority', although Portsmouth does charge CIL. The trigger (development creating new dwellings or the relevant floorspace threshold) should be stated.
issues.evidence: trigger_excerpt: 'submit the CIL additional information form alongside their planning application.'

issues.detail: Seven tab_items are process text, appeal and fee wording, or a list of download links, not validation requirements. They are: 'The Planning Inspectorate will consider the merits of the validation dispute...' (twice); 'The process for invalid applications is as follows:'; 'If after the 14 days ... refunded, minus an admin fee of 10%'; 'It is our aim to process new applications within 3-5 working days'; 'Please read the National ( ) and Local (see below) requirements...' (boilerplate with a stripped link); and 'Documents Flood risk - assessment and information form (PDF) Community Infrastructure Levy Form 1 (PDF)... Valid' (the page's download list, cut off mid-word).
issues.evidence: tab_items section 'Submission rules' and 'Local forms / checklists'

issues.detail: The web page and the 2024 PDF were both captured, so the same items appear twice with only dash/quote differences: block plan, floor plans, elevations, Habitat Regulations Assessment, the nutrient neutrality/Solent sentence and the Planning Inspectorate sentence. The first drawing-standards item also joins two separate requirements (the red-line access-land note from the location plan and the 1:500 block plan). 'Should show the original paper size.' is a fragment with no subject.
issues.evidence: tab_items 1 and 9, 5 and 10, 6 and 11, 19 and 22, 20 and 23, 13 and 15

issues.detail: Req. items (36) does not match the extracted data: there are 23 actual requirement rows plus 15 '(none)' placeholder rows (38 in total). The 'Validation list URL' is the landing page, not the checklist itself. The checklist Grokbot actually read is the PDF 'VALIDATION-CHECKLIST-FOR-PLANNING-APPLICATIONS-2024.pdf'.

summary: The live source could not be checked because the session's web-fetch and web-search budgets ran out, so it is unknown whether the July 2024 checklist is still current or what it omits. Grokbot's own extraction shows a wrong list date (should be 23 July 2024), Householder wrongly marked '(none)', most rows guessed into Full planning, many fragment triggers, and process and boilerplate text counted as requirements.

withdrawn_issues.detail: List date is 2024-07-01, but Grokbot's own date basis says 'adopted on 23 July 2024', so the date should be 2024-07-23. The July 2024 date may also be stale: the list was due for its two-year review in July 2026, and no newer version could be checked.
withdrawn_issues.evidence: reference_row: 'List date': '2024-07-01', 'Date basis': 'text: adopted on 23 July 2024'
withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: List_date is stored at month precision (YYYY-MM-01), so 2024-07-01 matches 'adopted on 23 July 2024' and the date is not wrong. Staleness is already flagged: the workbook marks Outdated='Yes' for every Portsmouth row.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. The workbook stores list dates to the month, so the value is right; only the date-basis label could be better. Not a Grokbot error. Outdated is already flagged.

withdrawn_issues.detail: Quoted triggers carry statutory references that are out of date, and Grokbot repeats them without comment. The BNG row says major development needed a Biodiversity Gain Plan 'As of the November 2023', but statutory BNG started on 12 Feb 2024 for major and 2 Apr 2024 for small sites. The EIA row cites the 'EIA regulations (2011)', which the 2017 Regulations replaced. Whether these errors are in the source or came from extraction could not be checked.
withdrawn_issues.evidence: 'As of the November 2023 all proposals for Major Development, and from April 2024 all proposals for Minor Development'; 'Town and Country Planning EIA regulations (2011)'
withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: This can be checked: both phrases appear in the captured source (raw 071016a1ec page and raw 3f0b5d21df/f8c09098be text: 'As of the November 2023…' and 'EIA regulations (2011)'). Grokbot quoted the source accurately, so this is a source-currency caveat, not an extraction error.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. Grokbot quoted the source correctly; the out-of-date references are the council's.
